# Resurf or Anybox? Both are native. They are built for different libraries

Anybox is a focused bookmark manager with excellent Apple automation. Resurf is a broader context library for links, notes, screenshots, voice, PDFs, media and files. Both respect the Apple ecosystem, but the overlap ends sooner than it first appears.

We make Resurf. Everything here comes from Anybox's own pages, we say where Anybox is ahead, and planned Resurf features don't count.

## The short answer

### Choose Anybox if you mainly save, organize and open links [...] Anybox currently lists monthly, yearly and lifetime options. Resurf has a free Mac tier and one-time Mac licenses, and the iPhone and iPad apps are free and unlimited.

The extra cost is easier to justify when you use voice, OCR, document search, mixed media, Ask Your Library and resurfacing. It is harder to justify if all you need is a place for links. Check both live pricing pages before deciding, because promotions and plan terms can change.

## Which should you choose?

### Pick Anybox for

 A focused bookmark and read-later app
 Nested tags and folders
 Smart lists and system-wide Quick Find
 Save All Tabs and browser-bookmark migration
 PDF, WebArchive and screenshot archive choices
 Deep AppleScript, launcher and copy-template support
 A lower-priced lifetime option

### Resurf, if you want to own your library

The one I make. Mac, iPhone and iPad, with everything stored as ordinary files on your Mac (markdown notes, original images and PDFs) and synced through your own iCloud. There is no Resurf account and no server of mine holding anything. On Mac it also searches by meaning and finds similar captures on the device (both Beta), and agents such as Claude, Codex and Cursor can search and read it over MCP.

The catch: Apple only, with no Windows, Android or web app planned, and no shared libraries. If you need any of that, pick one of the others above.

What is the best free alternative to mymind?
:   Raindrop.io, by a distance. Its free tier gives you unlimited bookmarks, collections and devices at no cost across every major platform, limited mainly by 100 MB of uploads a month. Karakeep is also free without limits if you are willing to self-host it on your own server.

Is there a mymind alternative that stores files locally?
:   Yes. Eagle keeps a local library on macOS or Windows, and Resurf keeps everything as ordinary files on your Mac. Automatic visual organization in a hosted service, or a private mixed-media library held on your Apple devices.
